adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
No comma before the et joining a two-member pair, with do and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.lavabo w024: semper et ubíque is one adverbial pair.
No comma before the apposition Dóminum nostrum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018 for the same closing formula.

House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals, and handmissal-eo attests the practice. Ángeli has three syllables and must show its stress.
No comma before the ac joining the third subject of concélebrant, with do: Cæli, Virtútes and Séraphim are one series of subjects.
No comma between the last subject and the ablative phrase that qualifies the verb, with do.
No comma between deprecámur and its object voces, with do and with the typical edition, which prints the comma only after jubeas.

Two accidental differences on one token, which the apparatus can label only once (a known limit, recorded in the backlog). The witness prints júbeas where this edition prints iúbeas — the j-for-i house rule, reversed 2026-08-06 — AND omits the comma this edition sets after it. Classed as punctuation because that is the difference a reader would notice; the orthography is the same rule applied everywhere else in this text.
Accented, with handmissal-eo and with the same do file's own confessióne in the Preface of All Saints: a word of four syllables carries its stress mark.
